validation_case.given: a linked worktree sharing core.hooksPath with its main checkout while generated hook environment is ignored per checkout
validation_case.when: the hook resolves its tool through a relative vendor/bin fallback or changes directory to the hook file's common checkout
validation_case.then: the hook can run the wrong root or fail to find the executable, so it resolves the current Git root and uses a pinned repository-local CLI path

content.title: Resolve the hook environment per checkout, not through shared hook configuration
content.context: Linked Git worktrees share `core.hooksPath`, while the generated `agent-loop-hooks.env` is gitignored and therefore exists per checkout. In a fresh worktree the pre-commit hook found no env file, ran `vendor/bin/agent-loop` relative to the wrong root and failed. Running `init sync-githooks` would have rewritten the shared `core.hooksPath` for every worktree.
content.guidance: In a hook, resolve the current checkout root with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` first and fall back to that checkout's own `vendor/bin/agent-loop` or `bin/agent-loop` when no generated env exists. Do not repair a single worktree by mutating shared `core.hooksPath`.
content.why_it_works: Every worktree then finds an executable CLI from its own root, and no worktree's fix changes what the others run.
content.when_to_apply: When a hook or its helper library reads generated, gitignored state, or when debugging a hook that only fails in a linked worktree.
content.when_not_to_apply: For repositories that never use linked worktrees and keep no checkout-local generated hook state.
content.symptoms: `git commit` in a new linked worktree fails inside the hook with `vendor/bin/agent-loop: No such file or directory`, while the main checkout commits fine.
content.root_cause: Hook configuration is shared across worktrees but the generated hook environment is checkout-local, and the hook assumed both lived in the same place.
